MINE BOMBERS 3.11
THE REMAKE

The 1996 DOS classic of digging, gold and dynamite - rebuilt instruction by instruction, then grown into something much bigger.

1-4 players, one keyboard 9 game modes 29 new bombs 17 new monsters 21 new tiles Bots · gamepads · replays Level editor

Mine Bombers is copyright Skitso Productions (1996). The remake, the level editor and the new graphics are by DarkSoL. Unofficial fan project, free to play and share.

118 847lines of the original program's disassembly, read line by line
57 000+lines of new C++17 code
3 100+automatic checks run on every build
25recorded demo matches replayed bit for bit
165settings, every one of them can be switched off

1. Quick start

  1. Unpack the folder somewhere you can write to (not into Program Files) and start MineBombers.exe. Nothing has to be installed: every library is next to the exe.
  2. On the main menu choose New game. The players screen opens: type names or pick saved players, then PLAY.
  3. With the Remake switched on, the Match setup screen follows: pick a mode and press F2 to start. With the Remake switched off you go straight to the shop, exactly as in 1996.
  4. Buy bombs in the shop, leave it, dig for treasure, blow up your friends. The richest player (or the last one standing) wins the round.
The game opens in a window at double size (640x480 is drawn, the window keeps the 4:3 shape and stays sharp). Want it smaller or bigger? Resize the window, or start MineBombers.exe --scale 1.

2. Two games in one: Clone and Remake

The program contains two games and you choose between them with one switch - REMAKE MODE at the top of the Remake screen.

REMAKE MODE: OFF - the Clone.
Mine Bombers 3.11 as it was in 1996: the same rules, numbers, random generator, shop, sounds and music, the same quirks. Nothing new is shown, nothing new is loaded. A file of settings that does not exist yet means exactly this.
REMAKE MODE: ON - the Remake.
Everything new switches on: content, modes, bots, interface, statistics, effects. Each of the 165 settings can still be turned off one by one, so you can play the original with just the bits you like (for example only gamepads and the item strip).

The core of the game never asks "is this the remake?". It reads a set of rules, and the rules with the switch off are by construction the original ones. That is why the clone stays exact no matter how much is added on top - and why the automatic checks can prove it.

Presets. On the Remake screen F2 cycles presets (from the plain clone to "everything on"), F3 switches everything in a section on or off.

3. Controls

Player keys (factory layout, as in the original)

Up to four players share one keyboard. Every player has seven keys: four directions, Stop, Bomb (drop / buy), Choose (select weapon / sell) and Remote (detonate remote bombs).

PlayerMoveStopBomb / buyChoose / sellRemote
1numeric keypad 4 6 8 2Num 5grey Page Downgrey Page Up / EnterNum 1 / End
2A D W XSTab`Z
3K ; O .LI8,
4arrow keys`right Ctrlright Shiftright Alt
Player 2 does not use WASD: S is Stop and down is X. And with the factory layout ` both stops player 4 and cycles player 2's weapon - that collision is in the 1996 original. Change anything you like on the Redefine keys screen.

Keys during a level

KeyWhat it does
PPause
F5Music on / off
EscEnd the level (two or more players). In Adventure: asks whether to leave the mine.
F10End the whole match
hold ChooseRemake: the item strip - a row of everything you carry; left / right scroll it, let go to pick.
M / QAdventure only: world map / quest list

Holding Bomb drops a stream of bombs - that is the original behaviour (the 1996 keyboard handler accepted every repeated key). The remake can make it one bomb per press, or keep the stream steady while you walk; see Gameplay options.

Gamepads

Up to four pads through SDL (Xbox, DualShock, DualSense and most others). Plug them in any time - even in the middle of a match.

  • Assign a pad to a player on the Redefine keys screen, the same way as keys: press the pad button when the row asks for it. Every button can be used: Cross, Circle, Square, Triangle, L1/R1, L2/R2, L3/R3, Share, Options, PS, touchpad (Xbox pads: the same places). Put Stop and Remote on buttons, not on "stick released".
  • In menus the stick and d-pad are the arrows, Bomb is Enter, Stop is back, Choose is Tab, and Remote opens the KEYS window with every other key a screen may want (F1..F10, Page Up/Down, Delete, letters...).
  • On a level and in the shop hold Stop for a second: the KEYS window offers leave, pause, map, quests, save and so on.
  • Match setup: START sits under the last row - press down to reach it.
  • Replays: left/right rewind and skip, up restarts, Choose pauses, Stop leaves.
  • Rumble: the pad kicks when a bomb goes off nearby.
  • Typing names and the level search still need a keyboard.

Mouse

With Mouse in menus on, menus, the Remake screen, Match setup, Load levels, the replay list, the quest board and the save panel can all be clicked; a double click opens a level or a replay. The shop deliberately has no mouse: with four people at one keyboard nobody could say whose mouse it is.

4. Menus and screens

Options (the original screen)

The original options are kept as they were and saved to the original 17-byte OPTIONS.CFG:

  • Cash - start money; Treasures - items on a random map; Rounds; Time limit of a round; Players (1-4); Speed (4-100); Bomb damage;
  • Darkness, Free market (random prices), Selling, Winner by money or rounds won;
  • REDEFINE KEYS, LOAD LEVELS, MAINMENU. D restores the defaults.

In the remake most of these are also shown and changed on the RULES tab of Match setup - both screens edit the same values.

Redefine keys

The original wizard walks through all 28 rows; press the key (or pad button) for each. Esc keeps the old key of a row, F10 saves and quits, F5 restores the factory layout.

Remake additions: the row being asked is highlighted, Backspace takes the last key back (in the original a mistake meant walking all 28 rows again), keys bound twice are shown in red, and pad buttons are accepted.

Load levels

Here you choose which map is played in which round. Every .MNE file in the LEVELS folder is listed; Random means a generated map. The right panel previews the map under the cursor.

KeyRemake addition
TabSort by name or by date (remembered)
/Search: type to filter the list
F / F2Mark a favourite / show only favourites (kept in favourites.txt)
F3Hide maps that need content you have switched off
F4Open the random map generator - its settings are used for every Random round

Over 300 community maps (made by players of the original in the late 90s, see LEVELS\COMMUNITY.TXT) are included next to the 61 maps of the original. The list holds up to 495 maps.

Info - the encyclopedia

The original Info pages (Weapons, Tools, Shapes, credits) are followed by new pages in the same style describing every new bomb, item, tile and monster. Space or any key turns the page.

The Remake screen

Main menu → Remake opens a small hub: Remake Options (every setting, section by section) and Replays. The options are grouped in six tabs - Content, Modes, Gameplay, Controls, Video, Audio. Left/Right switch tabs, Enter opens a section, Space changes a value, the line at the bottom explains the item under the cursor. The full list is in the Options reference.

5. Players and profiles

The original players screen: up to four names, a database of saved players (PLAYERS.DAT) and statistics with the history graph of each player. Type a name or pick one from the list.

Profile (remake). Put the cursor on a player and press F1: a full page about that player - records, matches and rounds won, kills per death, money earned, favourite weapon, best match, the last matches with place and money, the playtime in every mode and the titles (medals) collected. Profiles live in PROFILES.DAT.

6. Match setup

With the Remake on, every match starts here. One screen holds the mode, the rules, the players (humans or bots), the shop and what happens before each round. F2 starts, F3 restores defaults, F10 goes back to the menu. Everything chosen is remembered for the next match.

The five tabs

Shop options

  • Purchase limit - at most N items per shop visit.
  • Shop rotation - every visit sells a random half of the goods.
  • Mirror match - no shopping at all: everyone gets the same random kit of 30-50 items.
  • Item blacklist - goods on the list are never sold (and the generator can keep them off random maps too). The list is edited on its own screen: arrows move, Space bans or allows, F3 all, Esc done.

Map vote

Before the round (every round or only the first) three maps and RANDOM are offered. Each player picks with his own left/right keys and votes with Bomb; bots vote too. Most votes win; a tie is drawn by lot. Esc ends the vote early.

Draft

Before the round the players ban goods one after another - the player last in the score bans first. Banned goods disappear from the shop for this round or for the whole match (your choice), 1-3 bans per player.

Chaos mode

Every N seconds (10-120) a random rule takes over the round until the next one: DOUBLE DAMAGE, DARKNESS, MONSTER RUSH (a lively monster for every player), SUPPLY DROP, TREASURE RAIN, HEALING. The name of the rule flashes above the field.

7. Game modes

Classic 1-4 players

The original game. The last one standing or the richest wins the round. With one player it is the Original campaign: 15 levels that always play by their own 1996 rules.

Battle Royale 2-4

A purple storm closes in by phases; outside it you burn. Last one standing wins - treasures do not end the round. Phases, damage and when the zone becomes a point are settings.

Grail 2-4

One grail appears near the middle. Carry it to your corner; the first to N deliveries wins. The carrier walks at half speed, a lost grail returns, the fallen get up at their base.

Sandbox 2-4

Practice. Endless money, you get up after dying, the round never ends by itself, no scores or statistics are kept. Perfect for trying every bomb.

Team Deathmatch 2-4

Two teams; a team wins when the other one is gone. Team colours (six to choose from), coloured HUD, friendly fire full / half / off.

Co-op 2-4

All players as one team against the mine: collect every treasure or kill every monster. Extra monsters per player can be added on top of the map.

Survival 2-4

Monsters come in waves, each one harder. Live through N waves. Start in the corners or together in the middle, on a fresh arena; supplies after every wave.

Custom Campaign 1-4

Your own levels NAME0.MNL, NAME1.MNL... played in order - alone (with saves) or as one team with shared lives. Any player may open the exit.

Adventure 1 player

A huge random world of sand, solid rock and basalt, with ruins, camps, quests, loot and monsters - and a grail hidden far away. See chapter 12.

In team and co-op modes the outcome of the match is shared: all members of a team get the same final picture (win, draw or loss) and the same place in their profiles.

8. On the level

The basics

  • Dig by walking into the ground. Sand is soft, rock is hard, metal plates cannot be dug at all. Pick axes and drills raise your digging power for good.
  • Treasures are money: from a brass bracelet ($10) to a crown ($100) - and the rare diamond ($1000). Collected money is yours; what the dead leave behind goes to a prize fund.
  • Bombs are dropped where you stand and go off after their fuse. Remote bombs wait for your Remote key. Choose cycles your weapons.
  • Boulders can be pushed, security doors are opened by door switches, teleports carry you to another teleport, mines are invisible until someone steps on them, cracker barrels explode when hit, wooden weapon containers hold random armament.
  • The round ends when only one player is left alive, when the time runs out, or when nearly all the treasure is collected.
  • Darkness (option): you only see what you have seen. Eyesight (remake): darkness always, and you only see the way you are facing.

Remake helpers

  • Item strip - hold Choose for a row of everything you carry.
  • Floating numbers show damage, particles fly out of blasts, blood spatters in droplets, the screen shakes as much as you like (the original shakes only for nukes).
  • Camera zoom (single player): the field is zoomed in and follows you.
  • Fix player 4 death - the original never finishes off player 4 at zero health (a bug in the 1996 code). The fix is on by default in the remake; the clone keeps the bug.
  • Chain blast cap - the original draws a huge chain reaction to the end, however long it takes; the remake can cap how much of it is drawn.

9. The shop

Between rounds two players share the shop screen at a time (players 1+2, then 3+4). Move with your direction keys, Bomb buys, Choose sells (if selling is on), LEAVE (or Esc) goes on. Prices may change by up to 30% on every visit when Free market is on; selling returns 70%.

Saving a campaign

In single player (Original and Custom campaign) and in Adventure the shop has a SAVE / LOAD panel: several slots, each showing the player, money, level and date. A Custom campaign has its own slots. Co-op campaigns are not saved by design.

10. After the round

Round summary

After every round each player gets a panel with pages - turned with that player's own left/right keys; each player presses his Remote key when ready (bots are always ready).

Medals of the round: FIRST BLOOD, BUTCHER (most kills), SURVIVOR (never died while others did), MINER (most dug), RICH (most earned), EXTERMINATOR (most monsters), BOMBER, MEDIC, KAMIKAZE. A medal needs a non-zero first place; ties share it.

End of the match

12. Adventure

A single player mode with its own world and its own rules. You start in a small clearing of an enormous random mine and go wherever you like. Somewhere far away, inside an obsidian vault deep in basalt, lies the grail.

The world

  • Sizes: SMALL 256x180, MEDIUM 512x360, LARGE 1024x720, HUGE 2048x1440 and INFINITE. The same seed always builds the same world.
  • Three biomes: sand, solid rock and basalt - richer and more dangerous the farther you go (Danger by distance). Caves, passages, pools of water and petrol, webs, geodes, golden bags, rare diamonds.
  • Twelve kinds of structures in four sizes: hut, bunker, treasury, camp, base, warehouse, shrine, crypt, mine shaft, lab, powder store, outpost - intact, ruined or buried, with their own loot and guards.
  • Difficulty: PEACEFUL, EASY, NORMAL, HARD, NIGHTMARE (monsters already at the start, ambushes in the rock) and CHAOS - one roll for the whole world that goes past every limit.
  • You see a window of 64x45 cells; the world remembers everything you change, every monster you left behind and every cell you have seen.

Playing

  • Lives 1-9. You get up again at the last camp you visited. One life is a roguelike run: death erases the save.
  • Camps and bases hold the only shops. Inside: random prices, rotation and selling; the SAVE / LOAD panel; and the quest board. CONTINUE a saved world from Match setup.
  • Quests: kill, find, collect, dig, travel, visit a biome, deliver to another camp, and more - for money, score or items.
  • Dud bombs lie in the mine; step on one to take it.
  • Vision: DARKNESS (you see what is near) or EYESIGHT (only where you look). Zoom X2 with four camera styles, or X1 with the whole window on screen.
  • Grail compass in the status bar shows the direction and distance to the grail and to the nearest camp. M opens the world map of what you explored (7 zoom steps).
  • Score: treasure, monsters, structures found, cells explored, quests, and 10000 for the grail - multiplied by the difficulty.

13. Bots

Any player place can be given to the computer on the PLAYERS tab of Match setup, with three skills: Easy, Normal, Hard. Bots play every mode with two or more players.

How they think. A bot does not know the bombs by heart. It runs a copy of the world forward in time - the game is fully deterministic, so a copy costs microseconds - and simply watches where and when every blast will land. That is why bots understand all 29 new bombs, chain reactions, crusts and lava without a single line of code written for them.
  • They plan paths by time, digging included; wait out blasts; push boulders; use teleports, door switches and remote bombs; blow up brick walls that are cheaper to blast than to dig.
  • They chase treasure first, then weakened opponents; hold the Battle Royale zone; carry the grail; never hurt a team mate.
  • They avoid biting monsters and the line of fire of grenade throwers, and blow up dangerous monsters nearby.
  • They shop sensibly (digging power first, then health, tools and the bombs that pay off best), vote on maps and ban goods in the draft with some variety.
  • Easy thinks less often, ignores monsters and tools; Hard recomputes more often, attacks more and uses clones and super drills.

14. Replays

With Match recording on, every round is saved to the replays folder as a small file of keypresses (one file per round). The world is deterministic, so a replay shows exactly what happened - and every replay can be checked against the game.

Main menu → Remake → Replays: a list with date, players, round and length; Tab sorts, / searches, F marks favourites, F2 shows only them. Unreadable files are listed dimmed with the reason.

Watching: Space pause, Left/Right 5 seconds back or forward, Up to the start, Esc back to the list.

15. The random map generator

Press F4 on Load levels. The same generator lives in the level editor. Its settings are kept in gener.cfg and used for every Random round.

TypeWhat it builds
OriginalExactly what the 1996 game builds: tunnels through solid rock, corner tiles and 45 items.
CavesCellular automata: soft natural caverns; sand at the walls, rock deeper in.
MazeA perfect maze, every cell reachable; corridor width sets how open it plays.
RoomsRooms joined by L shaped corridors - always connected.
ArenaCaves mirrored, so every player starts on the same ground.
TunnelsLong burrows gnawed through solid rock.
IslandsOpen ground with ragged islands of rock - a map for shooting, not digging.
FortressRings of metal wall with gates and a vault in the middle.
BombfieldOpen field sown thick with barrels, mines and spent charges.
PrisonCell blocks behind security doors; one lever opens every door at once.
All typesEvery round a random type. SAME keeps your settings, SURPRISE and CHAOS roll them each time.

Settings: density and smoothing, corridor width, rooms and room size, items, monsters (original only or remake monsters too), boulders, crates, first aid, teleports, mines, barrels, spent bombs, new tiles, metal border, smooth corners, cleared start corners, use blacklist. Buttons NEW SEED, RESET, SURPRISE ME and CHAOS.

16. The level editor

MineBombersEditor.exe creates and edits maps. It writes plain .MNE (multiplayer) and .MNL (single player) files of 2970 bytes - exactly what the 1996 game reads - and saves into LEVELS\, so a new map appears in Load levels straight away. F1 shows every key.

Highlights

  • Pencil, line, rectangle, ellipse, flood fill, spray, picker; filled shapes; brush size; vary (random sand or rock variant per cell); smooth rock corners; mirrored drawing.
  • Selections: move, copy, paste, swap; undo and redo (200 steps).
  • Map actions: flip, rotate, border, smooth, scatter treasure, clear, shift with wrapping, export to BMP.
  • Zoom 1-8 with the wheel, grid, map characters, full screen, player starts and unreachable areas.
  • Checks warn about problems (no exit on a single player map, closed starts...) but never forbid saving - the game itself does not check anything either.
  • Stats: monsters, treasure value, diggable cells, sealed cells.
  • Ctrl+G the generator, Ctrl+R "surprise me", Ctrl+Shift+R the same in chaos mode.

19. About the project

How it was made

Mine Bombers 3.11 was written in 1996 in Borland Pascal 7 for 16-bit DOS. Its source code was never published. The remake was rebuilt from the program itself: the disassembly of MB.EXE - 118 847 lines of IDA listing - was read procedure by procedure, and every rule of the game was carried over to modern C++17 with a reference to the exact line it came from.

The rule of the whole project: invent nothing, guess nothing, adjust nothing. Only what was understood 100% from the listing went into the game; what could not be understood was not done at all. Every statement in the 42 technical documents of the project carries a line number of the original listing.
  • The same arithmetic. The Turbo Pascal random generator (multiplier 08088405h) with the same order of calls; the map in memory transposed exactly as in 1996 (col*45+row), so memory dumps can be compared byte for byte; movement of one pixel per frame; fuses in frames.
  • The same sound. All 12 samples and all 29 places that play them, the Gravis Ultrasound voice pools (the last call wins - and you can hear it), both S3M music modules (menu and game) through a player written for the project.
  • The same files. Maps of 45x64 characters, the 17-byte OPTIONS.CFG, 266-byte player records, the original key layout and joystick pseudo-scan-codes.
  • Checked from three sides: by every file name the listing mentions (that is how the second music module was found), by every string the game prints, and by every procedure the documents mention. Of the 422 procedures of the listing, all that touch game data are accounted for.
  • Checked by playing. The most real differences were found by the author playing the game by hand - wrong music in a menu, a frozen note on leaving the shop, keys of players 3 and 4 not working - and every one of them was traced back to the listing and fixed.

Accuracy

  • The core of the game (core/) has no graphics, no clock and no floating point - it is a pure, deterministic function of the input. Graphics, sound and input are a separate layer. That is what makes exact replays, bots that look into the future and the clone/remake split possible.
  • 3 100+ automatic checks run on every build (core, interface and editor). Every new check was first broken on purpose, to prove that it can fail.
  • 25 demo matches - from plain digging to nukes, chains, four players, bots, every mode - are replayed after every change and compared hash by hash, frame by frame.
  • The bugs of the original are kept in the clone, because the goal was accuracy, not improvement: player 4 is never finished off at zero health (the "reaper" gets player 3's address), the random level generator hangs if Random(1601) returns zero, the factory layout binds ` twice. The remake can fix the first one with a switch.
  • Only four small things are not from the listing - all hardware behaviour the listing cannot contain (the Gravis Ultrasound volume curve, an uninitialised voice, joystick axis units, two corners of the S3M player). They are marked in the code. The only number that could not be measured is how long the 1996 graphics library took to draw a frame; it was set by ear and matches the Speed slider.

The remake compared with the original

Original 3.11 (1996)Remake
Runs onDOS, today only in DOSBoxWindows x64 natively, sharp scaling on any screen, any DPI, Cyrillic folder names
Game modesClassic and the single player campaign9 modes: Classic, Battle Royale, Grail, Sandbox, Team Deathmatch, Co-op, Survival, Custom Campaign, Adventure
Content27 goods, 4 monsters+29 bombs, +3 items, +17 monsters, +21 tiles - each can be switched off
OpponentsPeople onlyBots on three skills that understand every bomb
InputKeyboard, analogue joystickKeyboard, up to 4 gamepads with rumble and hot plugging, mouse in menus
Before a matchOptions screenMatch setup, map vote, draft, chaos, blacklist, purchase limit, rotation, mirror match
Maps61 maps, 1 generator, external editor+300 community maps, 10 generator types in game, a new editor, search, sorting, favourites
StatisticsFinal screen, history graphRound summary with death and map replays, medals, match report, player profiles
Replays and saves-Every round recorded, rewind; campaign and Adventure saves
EffectsScreen shake on nukesParticles, blood, floating numbers, adjustable shake, smooth panning and distance volume, separate volumes, your own music modules
HelpInfo pagesInfo pages for everything new, item cards in the shop, this manual
Faithfulness-With one switch it is the original, bugs included
